subject.title: fix(acp): keep completed run-mode sessions resumable

question: Should completed parent-owned ACP one-shots retain resumable metadata after terminal cleanup when all capability, identity, readiness, ownership, and fail-closed gates pass?
rationale: The patch fixes demonstrated context loss, but it deliberately narrows shipped cleanup behavior created to prevent stale sessions from respawning or injecting output; tests cannot determine the intended long-term lifecycle policy.

options.title: Accept guarded retention
options.body: Resolve the conflicts, preserve every resume and ownership gate, refresh exact-head proof, and allow explicit parent follow-ups to resume completed one-shots.

options.title: Keep terminal cleanup absolute
options.body: Retain the current close-all one-shot policy and close this PR if maintainers prefer preventing any post-completion resumption over preserving backend context.

recommendation.title: Accept guarded retention
recommendation.body: Resolve the conflicts, preserve every resume and ownership gate, refresh exact-head proof, and allow explicit parent follow-ups to resume completed one-shots.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision hinges most directly on ACPX resume capability, runtime ensure behavior, and missing-target error semantics.
